sections.h2: The US reserve is far smaller than China's estimated stock

chart.title: China's estimated stock is several times the US reserve, which fell below 300M bbl
chart.sub: Reported or estimated stock, million barrels. China's figure is a third-party estimate; it publishes none.
chart.source: EIA; NPR; third-party estimates as stated in the post.

sections.means: The US reserve was drawn down by a 172M bbl emergency release, and it fell to its lowest level since 1983 in early August.
sections.todo: ISPRL should publish fill levels for India's three strategic sites, so the 39M bbl designed capacity can be read against barrels actually held.

sections.h2: Iran's floating crude alone is larger than the usual global pool

chart.title: Blockaded Iranian cargoes exceed the global floating pool seen in calm markets
chart.sub: Oil on idle tankers, million barrels. The Iranian figure is Iran-specific, not a global total.
chart.source: Vortexa, as cited in the post; calm-market range from the post's background.

sections.means: The US port blockade stops empty tankers returning for the next loading, so the pile-up grows even without new demand for the oil.
sections.todo: The IEA should publish a dated global floating-storage total, with its definition, in each Oil Market Report while the disruption lasts.

sections.h2: Strait transits fell from about 85 a day to 1 on 20 September

chart.title: PortWatch counted 1 Strait transit on 20 September against a baseline of about 85 a day
chart.sub: Daily Strait of Hormuz transits. US officials cited roughly 60 ships on a single day that same week.
chart.source: IMF PortWatch; US officials as reported in the post.

sections.means: The two readings come from different counting methods, and the post does not reconcile them.
sections.todo: IMF PortWatch should publish its Strait of Hormuz transit counting method alongside its daily figures, so the two readings can be reconciled.
